Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Global Consumer Brands Inc., or GCB as many of you know us, Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if you're using a landline or the button provided if on webcast. To withdraw your question, press star then two. We ask that you limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Vice President of Investor Relations.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Global Consumer Brands Inc.'s Q3 2023 results. With me on the call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Marketing Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking and are based on our current expectations and beliefs. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. Global Consumer Brands delivered a solid Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our brands and the strength of our team. We are navigating a dynamic environment—marked by moderating inflation, shifting consumer behaviors, and intense competitive pressures—and remain focused on executing our strategic priorities of premiumization, operational excellence, and sustainable growth.

Our discussion today will cover four key aspects: our overall financial performance, which showed balanced top- and bottom-line progress; brand performance and innovation, where our Power Brands continue to gain share through targeted launches; supply chain and operational efficiency, yielding meaningful margin tailwinds; and our outlook for the remainder of the year, underpinned by accelerating organic momentum.

I will now turn the call over to Michael to provide more detail on our financial results.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we delivered a solid quarter. Net sales were $2.85 billion, representing a 4.8% increase compared to the prior year, with organic sales growth of 4.2%, driven by a combination of 2.1% volume/mix and 2.1% pricing. This marks our third straight quarter of positive volume growth globally, ahead of our prior guide and reflecting a meaningful inflection from earlier headwinds amid peak inflation and downtrading. Gross margin was 45.2%, up 140 basis points year-over-year and 80 basis points sequentially from Q2, outperforming the CPG industry average of around 41% as reported by NielsenIQ benchmarks. This expansion marks our third consecutive quarter of improvement and puts us on track for our full-year guidance of 44.5% to 45.5%. Operating income was $425 million, up 12% year-over-year, and diluted earnings per share were $1.12, a 15% increase. We continue to manage our costs effectively and invest in our long-term growth initiatives.

Let me dive deeper into our gross margin performance, which came in at 45.2% and reflects a balanced playbook amid persistent macroeconomic headwinds. This outperforms peers and positions us at the high end of CPG leadership. Starting with the drivers: pricing actions were first and foremost, contributing about 320 basis points of uplift. We've executed disciplined everyday pricing across core categories—snack foods, beverages, household essentials, beauty, and personal care—averaging 8-10% increases since Q1 2022. In North America, our largest market at 55% of revenue, average unit retail grew 9.2%, outpacing category inflation of 6.5% per IRI data. This pricing power comes from strong brand equity in icons like PeakPulse energy drinks and PureGlow skincare, securing premium shelf space at Walmart and Kroger. Price elasticity has held favorable at -2.5 to -3.0, better than the industry norm of -3.5 from McKinsey studies, enabling cost pass-through without major volume loss. Net pricing grew 6.2% year-over-year overall, outpacing our 4.5% list price hikes, with targeted 5-7% increases on staples like laundry detergents and paper goods in North America yielding minimal pushback—volumes held flat ex-acquisitions, supported by our Everyday Rewards loyalty program boosting repeat purchases by 2%.

Offsetting these gains were input cost inflation and foreign exchange headwinds, pressuring margins by roughly 180 basis points combined, though we contained the drag effectively. Commodity baskets stayed volatile: cocoa surged 25% quarter-over-quarter from West African constraints, similar to challenges at Mondelez, while palm oil rose 15% due to El Niño impacts on Indonesian and Malaysian yields. In beauty, PET resin and fragrance oils added 10% to COGS. Year-to-date, key inputs like cocoa, sugar, palm oil, and corn derivatives—35% of our cost base—saw 45% spikes in cocoa from Ivory Coast and Ghana harvest shortfalls of 15%, and 12% sequential palm oil escalation from export curbs and biofuel demand. Overall input inflation averaged 8% YoY, but hedging limited Q3 drag to 40 basis points. We've secured 70% of 2025 cocoa needs at 20% below spot via fixed-price forwards and options with Barry Callebaut and Olam, and RSPO-certified palm oil contracts capped rises at 5%. North America gained from 10% lower corn futures on strong U.S. yields for salty snacks, while emerging markets like Brazil and India dealt with 15-20% higher sugar from weather disruptions. FX added a 50 basis point headwind, mainly from a stronger USD against the euro and EM currencies, hitting our 20% EMEA sales hardest. We expect commodity inflation to ease to 3-5% in Q4 absent Ukraine-related wheat flares.

Where we excelled was supply chain and procurement, delivering 200 basis points of structural expansion. Our Precision Sourcing program, covering 85% of global volume, uses AI-driven futures hedging and partnerships for 12-month contracts 5-7% below spot—like multi-year palm oil deals with Wilmar International for snack bars and soaps. Manufacturing optimizations consolidated three North American plants into two in Ohio and Texas, lifting throughput 18% and cutting conversion costs per case 12%. Robotic palletizers and IoT predictive maintenance reduced labor variances 8%, akin to P&G's gains. Zero-based productivity and AI formulation redesigns cut palm oil use 8% in spreads without taste compromise, prepping for EU deforestation rules. Sustainable sourcing now has 60% Rainforest Alliance cocoa, minimizing ethical premiums like Hershey's issues, and 40% overall certified.

Product mix shift added 90 basis points, with premiumization key. Higher-margin innovations like VitalRoots organic snacks grew 25% YoY, pushing premium SKUs to 35% of mix from 28%, mirroring Unilever's prestige moves but in mass channels. Power Brands now 65% of sales, up from 58%, with premium nuts/seeds up 15% in snacks, plant-based almond/oat milks at 22% mix in beverages delivering 300 basis points accretion via co-op deals, and eco-friendly cleaners gaining. We exited low-margin private label co-manufacturing in cleaners, dilutive by 400 basis points. Regionally, North America hit 47.1% margins, up 200 bps on pricing and trucking stabilization; EMEA at 42.8%, down 50 bps from Ukraine energy surcharges but offset by local wheat sourcing for baking mixes; APAC/LatAm combined 44.5%, aided by 15% volume in Indonesia/Brazil, with our Guangdong facility ramping for 50 bps more by Q1 2024.

Excluding one-time inventory normalization of 50 basis points, core expansion was 130 basis points from these levers: commodities stabilized via hedging, pricing capturing value with -1.8 elasticity, and mix elevating through portfolio shaping. We're piloting dynamic pricing with SymphonyAI for store-level optimization, eyeing 100 bps over 18 months, plus lapping Q3 2022 resets for 50 bps in Q4. Durable levers—procurement, footprint, premium mix—target 100+ bps annual expansion, like Colgate and Reckitt, with full-year core growth now at 150 basis points and 2025 at 44-45% via $200 million supply chain digitization.

Turning to the competitive landscape, which shaped our Q3 across beauty, personal care, household, and food & beverage amid 1.2% YoY U.S. food-at-home CPI, private label gains, and e-comm shifts. We've held 220 bps global market share stability per Nielsen/IRI against aggressive peers like P&G, Unilever, Reckitt, and Henkel.

On pricing/promos, P&G deepened EDLP on Tide Pods, cutting ASPs 4-6% for 1.8-point ACV in U.S. laundry per Circana; Unilever did Persil discounts in Europe for 120 bps household lift amid 2.5% deflation; private labels like Walmart Great Value hit 15% penetration growth, eroding branded velocity 3-5%. We optimized trade spend to 18% of revenue, down 50 bps, with high-ROI shopper marketing. U.S. Value Packs on EcoClean detergent at $0.09/oz recovered 150 bps share in 8 weeks at 2.1x ROMI per Kantar. Globally, ASPs +1.2% YoY via premium eco-variants at 15-20% premiums; AI dynamic pricing in 20% U.S. doors with Walmart/Kroger projects 50 bps 2025 uplift.

Innovation-wise, Colgate's probiotic toothpaste took 2.5 pts oral share in APAC Indonesia/Vietnam at 85% ACV; Nestlé's plant-based Garden Gourmet gained 300 bps Europe snacks vs. our protein bars on Green Deal claims. We countered with 12 NextGen SKUs, like microbiome serums lifting U.S. beauty penetration 8% per Numerator; R&D at 3.2% sales (up 40 bps) with AI cutting cycles 25% on sensory data, driving 4 ppt category outperformance and premium beauty to 28% mix from 22%.

Channels/regionally: North America Amazon/Walmart+ pressured us 1.2 pts vs. Native; we halved Amazon ACoS to 22%, growing e-comm 18% YoY. Europe Unilever's "Dirt is Good" NPS +12 pts; our €50M recycled PET pilot UK/DE resonated 68% with millennials per GfK, holding 32% share. EM locals like India's Dabur/Brazil's Natura took 3 pts beauty; we localized with guava shampoo at 92% Mexico distribution for 5 ppt gains, and WeChat minis expanded APAC share 14% despite P&G pods.

Strategically, premiumization targets 35% mix by FY25 (7% Euromonitor CAGR), blockchain sourcing via IBM cut stockouts 30%, ML promo forecasting at 92% accuracy. Our CPG 2.0 includes $250M clean beauty M&A and $400M zero-based reinvestment. Intensity peaked Q3 but we recovered 80% share; Q4 stabilization expected with 2-3 ppt FY gain on positive velocity and 115 NPS premium leadership.

Before Q&A, color on organic sales growth outlook, our core momentum measure excluding M&A/FX/divestitures for our 25 Power Brands like PureGlow skincare and EcoClean cleaners. Q3's 4.2% beat guide with 110 bps North America mass share gain in Beauty per Nielsen/IRI.

Q4 guide: 3.5% to 4.5% organic, with 1.8-2.3% volume/mix, 1.7-2.2% pricing. North America (55%): 3-4%, low-double-digit Health & Wellness volumes on VitaBoost probiotic snacks ($15B functional foods, 8% SPINS growth), PureGlow resilience, Costco/Sam's gains, 15% e-comm YoY despite Household flat laundry IRI. EMEA (25%): 4-5%, 2.5 pts Western Europe pricing lapping hikes, EcoClean refill promos (20% repeats), UK grocery +80 bps Kantar, euro FX watch. LatAm (10%): 7-9%, 4-5% Brazil/Mexico pricing on cooling CPI, mid-single SunnyFresh volumes, NielsenxAOC share vs. Coke/Pepsi. APAC (10%): 2-3%, China post-LNY Beauty, India 8-10% rural/JioMart, Indonesia hedging.

Underpinnings: 12 Q4 launches (40% plant-based Food/Beverage, 12% wellness CAGR Euromonitor), Velocity 365 +5% shelf/AI EDLP, e-comm 18% sales (up from 12%) via Shopify/TikTok Gen Z. FY2025 raised to 4-5% from 3.5-4.5%, Q4 acceleration, 2-2.5% volume/mix/pricing, $200M sustainability revenue (Walmart/Tesco recycling +15 YouGov equity). Resilient Growth: Power Brands 85% sales (6x category), SAP S/4HANA 3-4% productivity, $150M divestitures. Risks: cocoa +40% YoY, U.S. slowdown; insulated by 45% penetration, Essentials Tier vs. Unilever softness. Strong balance sheet (2.1x Net Debt/EBITDA), 12-13% EPS growth.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for Q&A. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of recent inflation trends on your consumer spending habits?

Sarah Thompson:
Thanks, John. Inflation has indeed squeezed wallets, with U.S. grocery up 4% per BLS, prompting some downtrading earlier this year. But our Q3 volumes turned positive, reflecting sticky demand for our value-for-money Power Brands. Consumers are premiumizing within budgets—VitalRoots organics up 25%, PureGlow serums holding despite private labels—thanks to household penetration at 45% and loyalty programs. We're insulated better than peers, gaining 110 bps share, and see stabilization as CPI moderates.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Johnson with JPMorgan.

Emily Johnson:
Regarding your new product VitaBoost probiotic snacks, what are the projections for its market impact?

Lisa Patel:
Great question, Emily. VitaBoost taps the $15B functional foods category growing 8% per SPINS, with low-double-digit volume expectations in Q4 North America rollout. Early doors show 8% household penetration lift similar to our beauty serums, outpacing category via microbiome claims and club channel velocity. We project $100M+ run-rate by FY2025, contributing 20-30 bps to organic growth, with AI-optimized formulations ensuring 25% faster market entry and premium pricing power.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley.

David Lee:
Can you provide more details on the promotional spending for the quarter?

Michael Chen:
Sure, David. Trade spend was disciplined at 18% of revenue, down 50 bps YoY, focusing high-ROI precision targeting versus broad discounting. We limited it to preserve ASPs at +1.2% YoY, countering P&G/Unilever EDLP aggression with Value Packs yielding 2.1x ROMI. In Europe, refill promos drove 20% EcoClean repeats; EM bundles on Shopee/Lazada added 9-11% pricing. AI tools optimized EDLP vs. high-low, projecting 50 bps uplift, while cutting low-ROI by 10% via zero-based reviews—freeing funds for innovation without share erosion.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Sarah Thompson for closing remarks.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Operator, and thank you all for your questions and participation in today's call. We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment—through pricing discipline, efficiency gains, competitive countermeasures, and a robust innovation pipeline—and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Global Consumer Brands Inc. Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
